evidenceClaims.statement: Inflammatory injury can increase alveolar-capillary permeability and reduce aerated, compliant lung in ARDS.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Hydrostatic edema can coexist; neither a positive fluid balance nor preserved ejection fraction independently classifies all edema.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Adult ARDS protective tidal volumes are indexed to predicted body weight, not fluid-dependent actual mass.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No newly invented anthropometric formula; checked PBW is supplied as a constructed record value.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: ARDS ventilation should limit tidal volume to a protective range of 4–8 mL/kg PBW and plateau pressure below 30 cm H2O.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Range does not prove every value is equally appropriate; initial target and pressure response require their own mappings.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: An initial low-tidal-volume target of 6 mL/kg PBW is used in the ARDSNet strategy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Historical protocol implementation, corroborated by current protective-range guidance; not a universal setting for every ventilation disorder.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: With ARDS volume already at 6 mL/kg PBW and plateau still above 30 cm H2O, the ARDSNet strategy reduces volume toward 5 then 4 mL/kg while reassessing gas exchange.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Constructed item excludes severe acidemia, patient effort and increased total PEEP; original Melissa hold remains. This is not authority for waiting for scale-weight loss.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: After protective settings and PEEP are optimized, persistent PaO2/FiO2 below 150 mm Hg on PEEP at least 5 supports prolonged prone ventilation in intubated adult ARDS.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Only one adequate independent guideline publication directly verified for exact eligibility; no fixed runtime wait or session duration taught. Contraindications still require clinician assessment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Routine prolonged high-pressure recruitment is discouraged in adult ARDS because benefit is not established and harm is possible.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Does not prohibit every brief recruitment maneuver for a discrete derecruitment event.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: During passive ventilation, an end-inspiratory hold measures plateau pressure and helps separate a flow-dependent peak-pressure increase from persistent static pressure loading.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Acquisition requires minimal patient effort and no major leak; unchanged delivered volume, flow and measured total PEEP are necessary for matched inference.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Visible artificial-airway secretions and compatible breath sounds support suctioning; adult patients should be preoxygenated for the procedure.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly verified society guideline; bronchoscopy remains appropriate for unresolved selected obstruction, not routine first secretion removal.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: In severe obstructive airflow limitation, incomplete exhalation can cause intrinsic PEEP; reducing respiratory rate can lengthen expiration and lessen trapping despite persistent hypercapnia.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Review directly supports the rate action; assessment guideline independently supports checking auto-PEEP. No numeric rate, safe pH or external-PEEP prescription is generalized.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: SBT readiness assessment considers recovery, oxygenation, hemodynamics and spontaneous effort; an RSBI calculation is not required to authorize a trial.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One direct guideline; no universal safety-screen cutoff authored. An abnormal isolated index is not a reason to bypass the rest of assessment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Increasing FiO2 during an SBT can conceal an oxygenation limitation, so the trial should generally retain its baseline oxygen concentration.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional very-low-certainty recommendation based on indirect evidence; repeat unchanged-support trial is a context-bound author application, not a universal extubation algorithm.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Tolerating an SBT does not establish readiness for extubation when weak cough and abundant secretions impair airway clearance.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline introduction directly states this boundary; no invented suction-frequency or cough-flow cutoff.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Bilevel NIV is recommended for acute or acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis from a COPD exacerbation in a patient not requiring immediate intubation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Direct pH at or below 7.35, elevated PaCO2 and persistent tachypnea support the constructed record; not extrapolated to every hypoxemic process.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Immediate clinical deterioration during an NIV trial requires prompt reassessment for invasive ventilation rather than extending the mask trial to normalize saturation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single joint guideline; key case has worsening consciousness, effort and acidemia together, not a universal pH-alone intubation threshold.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Preventive NIV immediately after planned extubation can benefit selected high-risk adults, including patients with chronic respiratory disease and hypercapnia.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional evidence; not a mandate for all extubations or proof of superiority to every modern HFNC/NIV combination. Options deliberately do not rank NIV against an equally supported high-risk HFNC regimen.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: NIV should generally not delay reintubation for established post-extubation respiratory failure in the general non-COPD, non-postoperative population.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional low-certainty guidance; COPD and postoperative populations are exceptions to generalization. Case uses medical pneumonia and worsening fatigue.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: An ordinary pulse oximeter estimates a saturation percentage; it does not measure blood hemoglobin concentration.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Device inaccuracies persist; a good signal does not independently validate adequate oxygen delivery.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Hemoglobin concentration determines available oxygen carriage, so a substantial fall can reduce oxygen content despite preserved measured arterial oxygenation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Qualitative inference from carriage and saturation facts; no numeric oxygen-content equation, tissue-delivery guarantee or demographic correction.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: For most stable hospitalized adults, a restrictive strategy considers red-cell transfusion below hemoglobin 7 g/dL in the clinical context.
evidenceClaims.limitation: AABB official summary is sole direct publication read for the exact threshold. Not a requirement to transfuse every low result, an outpatient-clinic transfusion rule, or a cardiac/orthopedic/ACS/major-hemorrhage protocol.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Oxygen delivery depends on blood flow and arterial oxygen content; a lower mixed-venous saturation despite improved arterial carriage and unchanged oxygen consumption warrants assessment of flow, not an assumption that normal SpO2 establishes adequate delivery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Physiologic author inference, not a diagnosis of cardiogenic shock or an instruction to give fluids/inotropes. No universal venous-saturation target asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Doppler echocardiography can assess stroke volume and cardiac output and can help characterize cardiac contributions to inadequate oxygen delivery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One adequate open review; does not establish every low venous-saturation result requires echocardiography before urgent clinical stabilization.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

evidenceClaims.statement: A humidification device can add resistive loading and increase peak airway pressure; a controlled device-dependent response can identify that contribution.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The second clause is an author inference from controlled fictional measurements, not a device diagnostic threshold. No waveform or comparative clinical trial is reproduced.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adult outside-hospital ventilation record reviewed retrospectively in the clinic; context-specific author application.

evidenceClaims.statement: Invasive ventilation requires ongoing humidification; active heated humidification is an available alternative when a passive HME contributes an ongoing problem.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The exact offered strategy is a context-bound application; no universal superiority over every fresh replacement HME is asserted. No temperature, humidity or replacement-time rule is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adult outside-hospital ventilation record reviewed retrospectively in the clinic; context-specific author application.

evidenceClaims.statement: An adult spontaneous breathing trial may use low pressure support or no pressure support.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional guideline recommendation; a specific unsupported trial must still be assessed for actual oxygenation, effort and circulatory tolerance. This does not establish a universal best support protocol.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adult outside-hospital ventilation record reviewed retrospectively in the clinic; context-specific author application.

evidenceClaims.statement: Preventive NIV after planned extubation is not routinely suggested for adults without a high-risk profile.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional recommendation with very-low-certainty evidence. Risk definitions vary; the revised item supplies its specific age/history and current readiness and does not extrapolate to COPD or postoperative exceptions.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adult outside-hospital ventilation record reviewed retrospectively in the clinic; context-specific author application.

evidenceClaims.statement: Improvement in pH and respiratory rate during an acute hypercapnic COPD NIV trial supports a favorable response when present clinical function remains suitable for continued monitoring.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One joint guideline directly verified for response direction. No universal observation time, PaCO2 normalization requirement or pH-alone success/failure cutoff is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adult outside-hospital ventilation record reviewed retrospectively in the clinic; context-specific author application.
